dataset.labelled_by: 20 public photos: AI draft corrected by a person. 16 own photos: described by a person first.

notes: Measures the damage reading only. Cost accuracy against real repair invoices needs the insurer's data.
The dollar gap compares the AI's estimate with the estimate priced from the human labels, using the same sample price table.
Each model ran twice per claim; the two runs are merged the same way the app does it.
The prompt was written on 12 other photos. None of the scored photos were used to tune it.
Small sample: one claim is about 4 points. Treat differences of a few points as noise.

ai_labelling.method: Four models from three providers (Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro (preview), Gemini 3.5 Flash, OpenAI GPT-5) each labelled every photo. They were given more than the app gets: the dataset's hand-drawn damage outline and its part labels. A finding is kept when at least two of them report the part; a part only one reports is optional. No person checked these labels, so they are reported apart from the human-checked results. The models scored on these labels are Claude models, and one of the labellers is also Claude, which favours them somewhat.
ai_labelling.note: Each photo is scored as a one-photo claim with no car and no accident description.
